title: Reflect fully, then choose
hookLine: the Gita's last instruction isn't an order: reflect, then choose
carry: the Gita hands the choice back to you
tomorrow: five years walked. what will you carry down the mountain?

cards: The night before someone leaves home, the advice comes in a flood: call, eat real food, don't trust that one friend. Near the end of the Gita's last chapter, Krishna has said everything he came to say.
Arjuna is still standing in the chariot, the armies still waiting. And the teacher's last instruction, in this verse, isn't another rule. It's a handoff.

teach.b: Krishna says: I have told you wisdom more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully. Then do as you choose.
A few verses later Arjuna answers: my confusion is gone. By your grace my memory has come back. I stand firm.
Memory, smriti, regained: not something new arriving, but something he had, returning. And what does he choose? I will do your word: he goes back to his dharma.
Many teachers read the verse as the Gita's trust in the student: a teaching isn't yours until you've weighed it yourself. A neighbor tradition ends its long teaching in a similar place.

Near the end of Deuteronomy, Moses speaks to the people before they cross the river: "I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live."

Shared: after all the teaching, the choice is put in the listener's hands, and the teacher trusts them with it. And an honest difference. Moses speaks to a whole people, and names his hope in the same breath: choose life.
Krishna's verse speaks to one friend and leaves it open; only afterward does he urge Arjuna to take refuge in him.
Five years on this path ran a little like that. First words, the stories, the Upanishads and the Yoga Sutras, the epics and the saints, the goddess and the schools, and this year the sources.
None of it came as a verdict to sign. It ends, as the Gita's verse does, with: reflect fully, then choose.

how: Some Hindus close a long stretch of Gita study by reading its last chapter, and some end each study session with a peace chant.

o: the year of reading the sources, at the summit
a year you choose one guru and take his vows
a review year that repeats year one in full

p: reflect fully, then do as you choose

s: the Gita's teaching ends with Krishna forbidding Arjuna to think it over
in 18.63 he says reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
Arjuna says his memory has come back
in 18.73: confusion gone, memory regained, I stand firm.
Moses and Krishna say exactly the same thing
both put the choice in the listener's hands; Moses names his hope, choose life, and speaks to a whole people.

games.q: the Gita's teaching is nearly done. what does Krishna tell Arjuna to do with it?
o: reflect on it fully, then choose.
keep it secret, never question it.
games.why: Gita 18.63: having told wisdom more secret than all secrets, Krishna says reflect on it fully, then do as you choose. Arjuna answers that his confusion is gone.

practice: Take a pen and write one line you're carrying down from this path: a word, a story, a sentence someone said. Read it once, slowly.
If you pray, you can offer it back with thanks; if not, let it rest on the page, the way Arjuna's memory came back.

wordCard.voice: Year 5: the year of reading the sources, ending at the top of the ranges with a handoff: reflect fully, then choose.

orig.note: Sanskrit: memory. In Gita 18.73 Arjuna says his memory has come back.

carryVoice: Your line: the Gita hands the choice back to you. Reflect fully, then choose. Five years, walked.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 18.63 (thus wisdom more secret than all secrets has been told to you by me; reflecting on it fully, do as you wish)
Bhagavad Gita 18.73 (Arjuna: my confusion is destroyed, memory regained by your grace; I stand firm, my doubts gone; I will do your word)
Bhagavad Gita 18.65–18.66 (Krishna urges Arjuna to take refuge in him)

sources.q: I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live
